title: Guide to the GBPA Arbitration Award
overview: This companion guide, published by the Government of The Bahamas, summarises the key rulings of the Partial Final Award in the arbitration against the Grand Bahama Port Authority. It explains the practical implications of the Tribunal's findings: that the GBPA must continue annual payments until 2054, that the Government retains legislative control over immigration and utilities in the Port Area, and that GBPA's claims to exclusive administrative authority were rejected. The guide is intended as a plain-language reference for policymakers, civil servants, and the public.
highlights: The GBPA is required to make annual payments to the Government until the Hawksbill Creek Agreement expires in 2054.
The GBPA's claims of exclusive rights over immigration, utilities, and administrative functions were rejected by the Tribunal.
The 1968 Supplemental Agreement remains binding and governs the GBPA–Government relationship alongside the original HCA.
The Government retains full legislative authority over immigration and utilities in the Port Area.
Only one aspect of the GBPA's counterclaim was upheld — regarding the Government's failure to approve environmental bye-laws in a timely manner.
